diagnosis.root_cause: The customer's receive optical power has steadily declined from the normal range (about -19.2 dBm) to the degraded range (-26.45 dBm), while fibre distance remains constant. TX power and laser bias remain stable and within normal limits, ruling out laser degradation or a path change. The elevated session count and short sessions are symptoms of the degrading optical link.
evidence: The target ONU is currently online and responding, so this is not an ONU-offline fault.
Peers on EPON0/3 have normal RX levels and remain online, isolating the issue to this customer's own path rather than the PON port, splitter, or OLT.
The seven-day RX trend starts in the normal band near -19.17 dBm and declines continuously to -26.45 dBm, ending in the degraded band; this meets the defined declining-link condition.
Fibre distance is constant at 188, so there is no path or record step change and distance_change is not indicated.
TX power stays near 2.3 dBm and TX bias current stays around 11.0-11.5 mA, both healthy and stable; this rules out laser degradation.
The current live RX reading of -27.1 dBm confirms the degraded optical condition.

There are 9 sessions in 24 hours with a 71-minute average duration, which is flapping-level behaviour, but the rules require the optical decline to be treated as the primary fault and the disconnects as its symptom.
OLT ping, SNMP, resource metrics, router heartbeat, VLAN assignment, and RADIUS records are normal, so there is no evidence of OLT, router, VLAN, or authentication failure.
The one offline peer is a separate single-ONU condition and does not affect the diagnosis of this customer's declining link.

remediation.action: Dispatch fibre maintenance for this subscriber path. Inspect and clean the ONU, patch-panel, splitter, and customer-side connectors; perform OTDR and optical loss testing; repair or replace damaged drop fibre, connectors, or splices as indicated. Recheck RX power and session stability after repair. Do not treat the healthy OLT, PON port, or router as the cause.

ground_truth.root_cause: Progressive attenuation in the fibre path between the splitter and this customer's ONU, consistent with a bend, damaged connector or degrading splice on the drop.
expected_reasoning: Cached RX of -26.40 dBm sits in the degraded band (-25 to -28)
Telemetry shows RX falling from -19.2 to -26.4 dBm over six days against a +/-0.3 dBm noise floor, so this is a trend and not a spot reading
Live RX of -27.10 is below the cached -26.40, so degradation is still progressing
TX power, TX bias current, supply voltage and distance are all flat, so the ONU laser and the fibre geometry are unchanged
Port neighbours on EPON0/3 read -19 to -22 dBm, so the PON port, feeder and splitter are healthy
The fault is therefore downstream of the splitter, in this customer's own fibre path
Nine sessions in 24h against a 2-3 baseline is a symptom of the marginal link, not an independent auth fault
Declining daily traffic is consistent with intermittent connectivity
distractors: Elevated session count invites a session_flapping_auth diagnosis
Declining traffic alone could suggest congestion
One neighbour (EPON0/3:21) is offline for unrelated reasons, at the 4.85% network baseline
